un-zi.draftGloss: Unzi (Langdon Un-zi) — first king of Akshak; UN + ZI; the sense of the name is not clear

un-da-lu-lu.draftGloss: Undalulu (Langdon Un-da-lu-lu) — king of Akshak; UN-DA-LU-LU; the sense of the name is not clear

ur-ur.draftGloss: Urur (Langdon Ur-ur) — king of Akshak; UR written twice; the sense of the name is not clear

šu-{d}šakkan₂.draftGloss: Shu-Shakkan (Langdon Gimil-ᵈŠaḫan) — king of Akshak; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + the god Šakkan (GIR₃, Langdon Šaḫan) with the divine determinative; not preserved on this prism, restored by Langdon from other copies

i-šu-il.draftGloss: Ishu-il (Langdon I-šu-il) — king of Akshak, father of Shu-Suen; I-ŠU-IL; not preserved on this prism, restored by Langdon from other copies

šu-{d}suen.draftGloss: Shu-Suen (Langdon Gimil-ᵈSin) — name of a king of Akshak and of a king of Kish; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin) with the divine determinative

in-ag.draftGloss: in-aĝ₂ (Langdon 'in-ag') — 'they ruled'; plural reign verb, a variant of ib-ag with -n-

x-šu-{d}suen.draftGloss: Shu-Suen (Langdon Gimil-ᵈSin) — king of Kish, son of Ku-Bau, and father of Ur-Zababa; on this copy a sign not identified (x) stands before ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin) with the divine determinative; the reading of the name is uncertain

ur-{d}za-ba₄-ba₄.draftGloss: Ur-Zababa (Langdon Ur-ᵈIlbaba) — king of Kish, son of Shu-Suen; ur 'man, servant' + the god Zababa of Kish, written ZA + the MUŠ₃ sign twice (read ba₄) with the divine determinative (Langdon ᵈIlbaba): 'servant of Zababa'

zi-mu-dar-ra.draftGloss: Zimudarra (Langdon [Zi-m]u-dar-ra) — king of Kish; ZI-MU-DAR-RA, the first two signs in the break on this copy; the sense of the name is not clear

u-ṣi-wa-tar.draftGloss: Usiwatar (Langdon U-ṣi-wa-tar) — king of Kish; U-ZI (read ṣi)-PI (read wa)-TAR; the first sign is in the break on this copy and the reading of the name rests on Langdon's

x-mu-ti.draftGloss: Ashdar-muti (Langdon Ašdar-mu-ti) — king of Kish; the first sign, Langdon's Ašdar (the goddess Ištar), is not identified on the copy and is shown as x, then MU-TI; the reading of the name is uncertain

iš-[…].draftGloss: Ish-… — the beginning of a royal name of Kish; IŠ, then a break (Langdon 'Ish-me(?)-', after the Scheil tablet's I-mu)

na-an-ni-ia-aḫ.draftGloss: Nanniyah (Langdon Na-an-ni-i̯a-aḫ) — last king of the fourth dynasty of Kish; NA-AN-NI-IA-AḪ; the Scheil tablet spells it Na-ni-ia-aḫ

lugal-zag-gi-si.draftGloss: Lugalzaggisi (Langdon Lugal-zag-gi-si) — the one king of the third dynasty of Uruk; lugal 'king' + ZAG-GI-SI; the sense of the rest of the name is not clear

a-ga-de₃.draftGloss: Agade (Langdon A-ga-dé; Akkad) — the city of Sargon's dynasty, in northern Babylonia; A-GA-NE (NE read de₃, Langdon dé) + the place-determinative KI, as a-ga-de₃{ki}
